title: Pair Parsing Run
statement: Let $C,e$ be natural numbers, let $m$ and $i$ be Boolean parameters, let $f$ map Boolean words to Boolean words, and let $h,w$ be Boolean words. Let $B$ be a natural number and let $v$ assign a natural number to each of fourteen registers, with every register value at most $B$. Suppose the register indexed by $1$ has value $v(0)+s|w|$, where $s=2$ if $i$ is true and $s=1$ otherwise, and suppose that for every $j<|w|$, the bit of $h$ at position $v(0)+sj$ equals the bit of $w$ at position $j$, interpreting out-of-range bits as false. If the aligned pair parser does not parse $w$, then for some $t\le |w|$ there is a bounded safe run from the configuration with state “scan” parameterized by $i$, register values $v$, and no result, to one with state “answer false,” register $0$ increased by $st$, all other register values unchanged, and no result. If the parser returns a pair $(a,b')$, there is a bounded safe run from that same initial configuration to one with the copy state at stage $4$ when $i$ is true and stage $0$ otherwise, register $0$ increased by $s(2|a|+2)$, all other register values unchanged, and no result.
